claims.statement: agent/dashboard/options.py is the single registry of selectable models: SUPPORTED_MODELS is a hand-maintained list of ModelOption records (provider-prefixed id, label, per-model efforts list, default_effort, supports_images), and SUPPORTED_MODEL_IDS is the frozen set every resolution layer checks membership against.

The efforts a model accepts are per-model and non-uniform: Kimi K3 and GLM 5.3 Flash only accept low/high/max while Gemini accepts minimal through high, and model_supports_effort/model_supports_images validate a stored selection against the model's own ModelOption fields.

Deprecated model ids are excluded from provider_fallback_pair and defer to defaults; DEPRECATED_MODEL_REPLACEMENTS has empty values, while unsupported non-deprecated ids may use same-provider and, where possible, same-Claude-family fallback.

default_model_pair() is the deployment-level terminal fallback: it reads LLM_MODEL_ID and LLM_REASONING_EFFORT, validates that the resulting model is supported and default-eligible, and raises ValueError for an unsupported model or effort.

For a hosted agent run, the factory seeds workspace main/subagent defaults, applies a profile only for a new snapshot or deliberate dashboard auto reset, then normally uses stored thread settings; a valid configurable agent_model_id/agent_effort replaces the main and subagent pair and the resolved settings are persisted back to the thread.

agent_overrides.resolve_agent_model_id resolves a supported per-thread id over a valid profile override over the workspace default, while dashboard thread-run resolution applies valid request pair over profile over workspace default and leaves the workspace default for a deprecated request.

Workspace role-default resolution returns a valid supported pair by taking a valid configured pair, otherwise same-provider fallback, otherwise default_model_pair; chat inherits the agent default when no valid chat-specific pair exists.

Effective workspace settings merge hardcoded defaults, the legacy instance record keyed default in the ['team_settings'] namespace, and non-null workspace overrides in ['workspace_settings']; failed store reads degrade to hardcoded defaults.

Workspace settings maintain distinct agent, reviewer, chat, routing-tier, and title model settings; title selection switches an OpenAI title pair to Anthropic when neither a usable gateway route nor OpenAI credentials or desktop OAuth are available.

Per-user profiles live in the ['profiles'] namespace holding main and optional subagent pairs plus repository, branch, and behavior preferences; the editable profile is deliberately split from encrypted GitHub OAuth token records in ['oauth_tokens'] so concurrent profile saves and token refreshes cannot clobber each other.

On the run-start path profiles are read fail-soft (agent_overrides.load_profile logs and returns None so a store blip costs only per-user overrides), whereas dashboard reads use profiles.get_profile so failures surface.

normalize_profile_overrides accepts a profile's default_model and reasoning_effort only when both are supported, default-eligible, and compatible; otherwise it attempts same-provider fallback for a non-deprecated stale id and returns (None, None) so the workspace default applies.

provider_model_kwargs translates a resolved effort string into provider-specific kwargs by dispatching on the model id prefix: OpenAI gets a reasoning dict, Anthropic gets adaptive/summarized thinking plus an effort field, Gemini 3+ gets thinking_level, Fireworks gets model_kwargs.reasoning_effort, and Baseten gets reasoning_effort for low/high/max.

make_model builds a chat model via init_chat_model and applies a default max_retries of 6 and a 600s per-request timeout for known provider prefixes so a stalled provider connection becomes a retry instead of a wedged run.

make_model configures OpenAI models for the Responses API with store=false, output_version responses/v1, and include reasoning.encrypted_content, and uses desktop OpenAI OAuth when no OPENAI_API_KEY is set and the gateway is not applied.
make_model routes Baseten as an OpenAI-compatible provider and, when the gateway is disabled, requires BASETEN_API_KEY and points at the Baseten base URL, raising if the key is missing.

Gateway routing is tri-state: a workspace gateway_enabled True/False is authoritative and None inherits the LANGSMITH_GATEWAY_ENABLED deployment default or dedicated gateway-key signal; when applicable gateway_overrides supplies base_url/api_key/use_responses_api, while absent credentials or unroutable providers fall back to direct calls.

fallback_model_id_for returns a cross-provider fallback for Anthropic and OpenAI primaries and None for providers that must not be silently re-routed; the factory honors LLM_FALLBACK_MODEL_ID first and ModelFallbackMiddleware alternates transient-error attempts across primary and fallback before surfacing an outage message.

Fable models are gated workspace-wide: disabling Fable rewrites stored Fable defaults to a safe non-Fable fallback, and the factory gates main, subagent, and title models while dashboard resolution and available-request options gate selections, preventing disabled Fable from being constructed or advertised.

Per-repo custom instructions are records stored in the ['agent_instructions'] namespace keyed by owner/name; the run factory resolves them for a new thread, persists them in the thread snapshot, and construct_system_prompt renders them as Repository-specific Custom Instructions shared by the thread.

Per-user custom instructions live in their own ['user_instructions'] namespace keyed by GitHub login and capped at 20,000 characters, so dashboard edits and agent save_user_instructions writes do not compete with profile persistence.

Prompt authority places AGENTS.md above repository custom instructions, workspace instructions, and personal standing instructions; personal instructions apply only when acting on their owner’s requests and are not transferred between senders.
For dashboard image-bearing run creation, a text-only resolved model is replaced with default_vision_model_pair; direct image-content validation rejects a missing or text-only model with HTTP 422.

Thread settings are a five-minute cached agent_settings metadata snapshot with typed fields for model, routing, and repository instructions; malformed snapshots load as empty, ordinary load/write failures are fail-soft, while strict writes re-raise.

Adaptive model routing starts from workspace routing tiers and can perform a one-time eligible dashboard or Slack requested-model handoff; the handoff validates availability, effort, and image support, then strictly persists model_handoff_complete and requested_model, while explicit selection disables routing.
